title: Flexbox alignment and wrapping
summary: Space and align flex items with justify-content, align-items and gap, and let them wrap onto new lines.

docs.title: MDN: Aligning items in a flex container

quiz.q: In a row flex container, which property spreads items along the **horizontal** main axis?
quiz.explain: `justify-content` works on the main axis (horizontal for a row). `align-items` works on the cross axis (vertical for a row).

quiz.q: Push the first item to the left edge and the last to the right edge, with the rest spread between.
quiz.explain: `space-between` puts equal gaps between items and none at the ends. Other values: `flex-start`, `center`, `flex-end`, `space-around`, `space-evenly`.

options: It lets items move to a new line when there is not enough room
quiz.explain: By default, flex items try to stay on one line and shrink. With `wrap`, extra items drop to the next line.

quiz.q: What does `gap: 16px` on a flex container do?
options: Adds 16px of space between the items
quiz.explain: `gap` adds space only between items, not at the outer edges, which is simpler than margins.

quiz.q: In a row container, which property vertically centres the items? Type just the property and value, for example `a: b`.
quiz.explain: `align-items: center` centres items on the cross axis, which is vertical in a row.

exercise.task:
Style a toolbar and a tag list. Work in `index.html`.

- `.toolbar`: `display: flex`, `justify-content: space-between`, `align-items: center`, `gap: 16px`.
- `.tags`: `display: flex`, `flex-wrap: wrap`, `gap: 8px`.
hints: Both containers need display: flex first. Then add the alignment and wrapping properties.
justify-content works along the main axis, align-items across it. flex-wrap lets items continue on a new line.

checks.name: .tags is a flex container that wraps
checks.hint: Add display: flex; and flex-wrap: wrap; to .tags.
